_comment: MLPR's own aircraft-type-to-icon table. Hand-authored by this project from public ICAO type-designator conventions, NOT a redistribution of any external ICAO/tar1090/BaseStation type database -- see CLAUDE.md's icon classification section for why. 'exact' always wins over 'prefix'; prefixes are tried longest-first and must be at least 3 characters (a 2-char prefix is never safe -- see the collision notes below). Stage 3 expanded pass (2026-07-29): broadened from Stage 1/2's ~30-entry illustrative sample toward real-world coverage for a Central/Eastern European receiver -- mainline/regional airliners, common GA/bizjet/helicopter types, and NATO/Polish military types. Several entries (noted inline) are lower-confidence designators recalled from general aviation knowledge rather than verified against a canonical source -- Stage 4's tools/ cross-check script (not built yet) is meant to catch any that are wrong; a wrong code is harmless on its own (it just never matches), so err toward including a plausible one over leaving a real, common local type unclassified.
_collisionNotes: Before adding any prefix, check it doesn't also match a type in a different icon category. Known traps: 'A3' catches both A30B/A306/A310 (widebody2) AND A318-A321 (narrowbody) -- split into 'A31'-family exacts plus separate 'A32'/'A33'/'A34'/'A35'/'A38' prefixes, never a bare 'A3'. 'C1' catches both C130/C160/C17 (military transports) AND C152/C172/C182/C206/C208 (Cessna singles) -- never used, both families are exact-only or use a longer, safe prefix (Cessna TWINS use safe 3-char prefixes like 'C31'/'C40' instead, which don't collide with the C1-family single/military codes). 'B7' catches both B73x (narrowbody) AND B74x/B76x/B77x/B78x (widebody) -- only used at 3 chars (B73/B74/B76/B77/B78), never as bare 'B7'.

military._comment: Consulted ONLY when the aircraft's dbFlags military bit is set, and ONLY for type designators that are genuinely ambiguous between a civilian and a government/military airframe using the SAME type code. These two entries are illustrative placeholders (A330/747 airframes are sometimes reused as tankers/AWACS-derivatives under their base civilian type code in some databases) -- verify against real data (Stage 4's tools/ script, plus manual spot-checking) before trusting them. Dedicated military tankers/AWACS/transports with their OWN unique type code (KC-135, E-3 Sentry, KC-10, KC-46...) deliberately do NOT need this table at all -- they'd just be regular exact entries in the table above, same as any other aircraft. None were added in the Stage 3 pass: their exact ICAO designators weren't recalled with enough confidence to include responsibly, left as a documented gap for Stage 4 rather than guessed.
